pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds a NOT NULL column defaulting to 'normal' with a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks the seeded rows are all normal and that 'urgent' is rejected. The test DB is built from the real migrations, so the seeded rows really are upgraded.
src/index.js `item()` appends ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. 'AC-2' asserts the exact <li> text.
src/index.js uses a bound `WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id` query. 'AC-3' asserts the contents and order for high, low and normal.
The unfiltered query is `ORDER BY id`. 'AC-4' asserts the full list in order.
`nav()` renders all four filters and shows the current one as <strong>. 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views.
Any `priority` param not in the set, including an empty one, returns 400 before any query runs. 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks there is no <li>.
A non-empty table with no match gives `No ${priority}-priority items.`; an empty table gives 'No items yet.'. 'AC-7' covers both, in every view.

traffic/routes.json is ["/", "/?priority=high"]. The 'AC-8' test would fail without that entry. The traffic Worker passes path+query to the app, and scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts a query string, covered in tests/traffic-config.test.sh.

findings.what: Line 87 is a blank line directly after `describe("states", () => {`. Prettier removes it, and `npm run lint` runs `prettier --check .`. Lint is a required CI check, so it would likely fail. I could not run lint to confirm.
findings.fix: Delete the blank line at line 87, or run `npm run format`.

findings.what: The 400 test checks the status and that there is no <li>. It does not check that the database is never queried, or that a HEAD request behaves the same way.
findings.fix: Optional: also assert the response body or a HEAD request.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec and its two decisions, and adds nothing beyond the ask. The checker regex change for query strings is needed by AC-8 and is stated in the PR.
All eight acceptance items are implemented and have tests that would fail if the behaviour broke.
The new tests assert behaviour. No test was deleted or loosened. The traffic fake and the checker tests were extended.
README.md describes the filter and `traffic/routes.json`. CLAUDE.md needs no change.
The query is parameterised, and bad values are rejected against an allow-list. One finding: a blank line Prettier would flag.
Input is validated against an allow-list, bound in SQL, and titles are HTML-escaped. No secrets or planted instructions found.
The page is plain server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or client code. I judged it not a UI change that needs design review.
There is no browser session and no screenshots in this change; the HTML is covered by the Workers-runtime tests.

The title is under 72 characters and the claims match the diff. The PR says the traffic-check script and its test changed, and both files show it. CI and the reviewer verdict are not checkable from the repo.
